Last updated 15 October 2026.

SelfHostAI is free to use. To help pay for it, some links may be **affiliate or referral links**. If you click one and sign up or buy, we may earn a commission or credit, at no extra cost to you.

## How we label them

- Every affiliate or referral link is marked Affiliate link next to the link itself, not only on this page.
- These links carry rel="sponsored" so search engines know they are paid links.
- **Featured listings.** If we sell featured listings in future, they will be labelled 'Featured' or 'Sponsored'.

## What it does not change

Commissions never change calculator results, figures, rankings or what we write. Tool details come from each project's public GitHub repository. We only link to services we think are relevant, and you can always go to a provider directly instead.

## Current partners

We list partner links only once a programme has approved us. Right now there are none.

This follows the UK CAP Code and ASA guidance that marketing must be obviously identifiable. See also our [privacy notice](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/privacy.html).

# Best self-hosted ChatGPT alternatives (2026) | SelfHostAI

Source: https://ai.andreiturcea.com/best-self-hosted-chatgpt-alternatives.html
Last updated: 2026-10-15


**Short answer:** The most common self-hosted ChatGPT alternative is Ollama (to run models) plus Open WebUI (the chat interface); LibreChat suits multi-provider setups, AnythingLLM chatting with documents, and Jan a desktop app with no server.

Last updated: 15 October 2026 · No tax figures on this site, so no GOV.UK check applies; tool details come from each project's public GitHub repository · [Markdown version](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/best-self-hosted-chatgpt-alternatives.html.md)

A self-hosted ChatGPT setup needs two parts: a **model runtime** and a **chat interface**.

| Tool | Type | Licence | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Open WebUI](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-open-webui.html) | Chat UI | BSD-3 | ChatGPT-style UI for Ollama and APIs |
| [LibreChat](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-librechat.html) | Chat UI | MIT | Multi-provider chat with agents |
| [AnythingLLM](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-anything-llm.html) | RAG app | MIT | Chat with your documents |
| [Jan](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-jan.html) | Desktop app | Apache-2.0 | Offline, no server |
| [Ollama](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-ollama.html) | Runtime | MIT | One-command local models |

## What does a typical self-hosted stack look like?

Laptop: Jan, or Ollama + Open WebUI. Small team on a VPS: Ollama or [vLLM](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-vllm.html) + LibreChat or Open WebUI, with [Langfuse](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-langfuse.html) for observability. See [Ollama vs llama.cpp vs vLLM](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/ollama-vs-llama-cpp-vs-vllm.html).

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the easiest self-hosted ChatGPT alternative?

For a single machine, Ollama to run models plus Open WebUI as the chat interface is the most common setup. Jan is a desktop app if you do not want Docker.

### Do I need a GPU?

Not for small quantised models: llama.cpp and Ollama can run them on CPU, but slowly. For larger models or several users, a GPU makes a big difference.

### Can I use cloud APIs from the same interface?

Yes. Open WebUI, LibreChat and AnythingLLM can connect to OpenAI-compatible APIs as well as local models.

Last updated 15 October 2026.

**SelfHostAI does not set any cookies** and does not use similar technologies such as local storage, tracking pixels or fingerprinting. There is no analytics or advertising code on the site, so there is no cookie banner.

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which serves static files and does not set cookies on these pages. If you click through to another site (for example Gumroad, GitHub or a partner), that site may set its own cookies under its own policy once you are there.

If this ever changes, for example if we add analytics or ads, we will list every cookie here and ask for your consent before setting any that are not strictly necessary, as the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR) require. See also our [privacy notice](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/privacy.html).

<!-- https://ai.andreiturcea.com/ollama-vs-llama-cpp-vs-vllm.html -->
# Ollama vs llama.cpp vs vLLM: which local LLM runtime? | SelfHostAI

Source: https://ai.andreiturcea.com/ollama-vs-llama-cpp-vs-vllm.html
Last updated: 2026-10-15


**Short answer:** Use Ollama for the easiest local setup, llama.cpp for CPU, edge devices and fine control, and vLLM for high-throughput GPU serving to many users.

Last updated: 15 October 2026 · No tax figures on this site, so no GOV.UK check applies; tool details come from each project's public GitHub repository · [Markdown version](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/ollama-vs-llama-cpp-vs-vllm.html.md)

|  | [Ollama](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-ollama.html) | [llama.cpp](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-llama.cpp.html) | [vLLM](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-vllm.html) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best for | Easiest local setup | CPU, edge devices, full control | High-throughput GPU serving |
| Hardware | CPU or GPU | CPU or GPU | GPU |
| Licence | MIT | MIT | Apache-2.0 |
| Repo | [ollama/ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama) | [ggml-org/llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | [vllm-project/vllm](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) |

Rule of thumb: start with Ollama, drop to llama.cpp when you need fine control or very low resources, and move to vLLM when many users hit one GPU server. [LocalAI](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-localai.html) is another OpenAI-compatible option. Add a UI from the [ChatGPT alternatives](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/best-self-hosted-chatgpt-alternatives.html) list.

## Frequently asked questions

### Should I use Ollama or llama.cpp?

Ollama is easier: one command to pull and run models, with an API. llama.cpp is the lower-level C/C++ engine, which gives more control and runs well on CPU.

### When should I use vLLM?

When you serve many concurrent requests on a GPU. vLLM is built for high-throughput serving rather than single-user desktop use.

### Do they offer an OpenAI-compatible API?

All three can expose an HTTP API that many OpenAI-compatible clients can use. Check each project's docs for the exact endpoints.


<!-- https://ai.andreiturcea.com/open-webui-vs-librechat-vs-anythingllm.html -->
# Open WebUI vs LibreChat vs AnythingLLM (self-hosted chat UIs) | SelfHostAI

Source: https://ai.andreiturcea.com/open-webui-vs-librechat-vs-anythingllm.html
Last updated: 2026-10-15


**Short answer:** Open WebUI is the usual ChatGPT-style UI for Ollama, LibreChat is best for mixing many API providers with agents, and AnythingLLM is built around chatting with your documents (RAG).

Last updated: 15 October 2026 · No tax figures on this site, so no GOV.UK check applies; tool details come from each project's public GitHub repository · [Markdown version](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/open-webui-vs-librechat-vs-anythingllm.html.md)

|  | [Open WebUI](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-open-webui.html) | [LibreChat](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-librechat.html) | [AnythingLLM](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-anything-llm.html) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Focus | ChatGPT-style UI, Ollama-friendly | Multi-provider chat + agents | All-in-one RAG over documents |
| Licence (as listed) | BSD-3 | MIT | MIT |
| Repo | [open-webui](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) | [LibreChat](https://github.com/danny-avila/LibreChat) | [anything-llm](https://github.com/Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm) |

All three run in Docker on a modest VPS. The model runtime is the heavy part: see [runtimes compared](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/ollama-vs-llama-cpp-vs-vllm.html). For document search at scale add [Qdrant](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-qdrant.html).

## Frequently asked questions

### Open WebUI or LibreChat?

Open WebUI is the usual choice alongside Ollama for a polished single-team UI. LibreChat is strong when you mix many API providers and want agents.

### What about chatting with my documents?

AnythingLLM is built around RAG over your files. Open WebUI also offers document features. For a vector database, see Qdrant.

### Which is fully MIT licensed?

LibreChat and AnythingLLM are listed as MIT. Open WebUI is listed as BSD-3; check its repository for any branding terms.

# Privacy | SelfHostAI

Source: https://ai.andreiturcea.com/privacy.html
Last updated: 2026-10-15


**Short answer:** Privacy notice for SelfHostAI: no analytics, no ads, no personal data collected.

Last updated: 15 October 2026 · No tax figures on this site, so no GOV.UK check applies; tool details come from each project's public GitHub repository · [Markdown version](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/privacy.html.md)

Last updated 15 October 2026. This notice explains what happens to your information when you use SelfHostAI.

## The short version

We do not ask for your name or email, we do not run analytics or advertising, and we do not set cookies. Anything you type into a calculator or filter box stays in your browser and is not sent to us.

## What is collected

- **Hosting.** The site is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages. Like any web host, GitHub receives technical data such as your IP address and browser details when your browser requests a page, and may keep it in server logs for security. See the [GitHub Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement). We cannot see those logs.
- **Calculators and filters.** These run entirely in your browser with JavaScript. Nothing is stored or transmitted.
- **Links to other sites.** When you follow a link to another site (for example GOV.UK, GitHub or a partner), that site's own privacy policy applies.

## Changes

If we ever add analytics, a newsletter, ads or anything else that collects personal data, we will update this page and the [cookies page](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/cookies.html) first, and ask for consent where the law requires it.

## Your rights and contact

Under UK GDPR you have rights over your personal data, including access and deletion. As we hold no personal data from browsing, there is normally nothing for us to give you. To get in touch, open an issue on the site's [GitHub repository](https://github.com/andreiturcea-creator/selfhost-ai-dir/issues) (issues are public, so do not include private details). You can also complain to the [Information Commissioner's Office](https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/).

# Dify: self-hosting guide & alternatives | SelfHostAI

Source: https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-dify.html
Last updated: 2026-10-15


**Short answer:** How to self-host Dify: requirements, licence and alternatives.

Last updated: 15 October 2026 · No tax figures on this site, so no GOV.UK check applies; tool details come from each project's public GitHub repository · [Markdown version](https://ai.andreiturcea.com/tool-dify.html.md)

LLM app and agent builder platform.

| Category | Agent builder |
|---|---|
| Licence | Apache-2.0 (modified) |
| Repo | [langgenius/dify](https://github.com/langgenius/dify) |

## How do you self-host it?

See the official README for Docker or binary install. A 2 vCPU / 4 GB VPS runs most UIs; LLM runtimes need a GPU or must run small quantised models on CPU.

## What are the alternatives?

Flowise
